glosses.notes: Used for describing a person, scene, process, or event in words.

examples.sentence: 请你先描述一下事情的经过。
他把自己的想法描述得很清楚。
这本书描述了普通人的生活。

example_translations.translation: Please first describe what happened.
He described his ideas very clearly.
This book depicts the lives of ordinary people.

glosses.notes: Can describe a body part that reacts easily, a person who notices small changes quickly, or a topic that feels delicate.

examples.sentence: 她的皮肤很敏感，太阳一晒就红。
他对数字很敏感，一看就发现了问题。
这个问题比较敏感，大家都不愿意多说。

example_translations.translation: Her skin is sensitive; it turns red as soon as it gets sun.
He is very quick to notice numbers and spotted the problem at a glance.
This issue is rather sensitive, and nobody wants to say much more about it.

glosses.notes: A formal word for the name of a person, thing, group, or program, especially in written or official contexts.

examples.sentence: 这个节目的名称后来改了。
请先写清楚公司的完整名称。
很多人知道这家店，却说不出它的正式名称。

example_translations.translation: The name of this program was changed later.
Please write the company's full name clearly first.
Many people know this shop, but they cannot say its official name.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to a famous brand or a name-brand product that people recognize.

examples.sentence: 他买衣服时不太看名牌。
这家商场卖不少国外名牌。
在她看来，东西好用比是不是名牌更重要。

example_translations.translation: He doesn't pay much attention to name brands when buying clothes.
This mall sells quite a few foreign name brands.
In her view, whether something works well matters more than whether it is a name brand.

glosses.notes: A small card with someone's name and contact details, usually exchanged at work.

examples.sentence: 他开会前先给了我一张名片。
这张名片上只有名字，没有电话。
我回到家才发现名片忘在办公室了。

example_translations.translation: He handed me a business card before the meeting.
This business card has only a name on it and no phone number.
I didn't realize until I got home that I had left the business card at the office.

glosses.notes: Can mean that something is clear and specific, or that someone makes responsibilities, goals, or rules clear.

examples.sentence: 老师把要求说得很明确。
现在意思已经很明确了。
开会前先明确一下谁负责这个部分。

example_translations.translation: The teacher explained the requirements very clearly.
The meaning is very clear now.
Before the meeting, let's first make clear who is responsible for this part.

glosses.notes: Describes something that is easy to notice, and it is also often used adverbially to mean noticeably or clearly.

examples.sentence: 这两张照片有明显区别。
他的中文明显比去年好了。
这个办法用了以后，效果很明显。

example_translations.translation: There is an obvious difference between these two photos.
His Chinese is obviously better than last year.
After this method was used, the effect was very noticeable.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to a well-known entertainer or sports star who is widely recognized.

examples.sentence: 这个节目请了很多明星。
她小时候一直想当明星。
那位明星一出现，大家就开始拍照。

example_translations.translation: This program invited many celebrities.
She always wanted to become a star when she was little.
As soon as that star appeared, everyone started taking pictures.

glosses.notes: A common noun for life itself, and in everyday speech it can also refer to a person's fate or luck in life.

examples.sentence: 这次手术救了他的命。
她觉得自己命很好，总有人帮助她。
关键时候，命比钱更重要。

example_translations.translation: This operation saved his life.
She feels her fate is kind to her, and there is always someone to help her.
At a critical moment, life is more important than money.

glosses.notes: Refers to the course a life seems set to take, or the fate that shapes what happens to someone.

examples.sentence: 这次机会改变了他的命运。
她相信命运，也相信努力。
小说里的两个人有完全不同的命运。

example_translations.translation: This opportunity changed his fate.
She believes in fate, and she also believes in hard work.
The two people in the novel have completely different destinies.

glosses.notes: Means to touch something with the hand, and it can also mean to feel around for something when you cannot see well.

examples.sentence: 博物馆里的东西不能随便摸。
天太黑了，他只好摸着墙往前走。
我在包里摸了半天才找到钥匙。

example_translations.translation: You can't touch the things in the museum casually.
It was too dark, so he had to feel his way forward along the wall.
I felt around in my bag for quite a while before finding the key.

glosses.notes: Can describe an image, memory, or meaning that is not clear, and it can also mean to make something look blurred.

examples.sentence: 字太模糊了，我看不清楚。
他的回答很模糊，我还是没听懂。
眼泪一下模糊了她的目光。

example_translations.translation: The writing is too blurry, and I can't read it clearly.
His answer was very vague, and I still didn't understand.
Tears suddenly blurred her vision.

glosses.notes: Refers to a fixed way something works, is organized, or is set up.

examples.sentence: 这家店想换一种经营模式。
手机现在是飞行模式。
他不想再重复以前的生活模式。

example_translations.translation: This shop wants to switch to a different business model.
The phone is in airplane mode now.
He doesn't want to keep repeating his old pattern of life.

glosses.notes: Describes a person, place, word, or feeling that is not known well and therefore feels strange.

examples.sentence: 第一次来这里的时候，一切都很陌生。
刚到新公司的时候，他对谁都很陌生。
这个词对现在的年轻人已经不陌生了。

example_translations.translation: When I first came here, everything felt unfamiliar.
When he first arrived at the new company, everyone felt unfamiliar to him.
This word is no longer unfamiliar to young people today.

glosses.notes: A formal word placed before a noun to mean a certain person, place, time, or group without naming it directly.

examples.sentence: 某天晚上，他突然收到一条短信。
这件事和某个人的决定有关。
新闻里没有公开某公司的名称。

example_translations.translation: One evening, he suddenly received a text message.
This matter is connected to a certain person's decision.
The news report did not make a certain company's name public.

glosses.notes: Can mean where someone's eyes are directed, and it can also refer to the feeling or attention shown in someone's eyes.

examples.sentence: 她的目光一直停在窗外。
她的目光里全是希望。
大家的目光都落在那张照片上。

example_translations.translation: Her gaze stayed fixed outside the window.
Her eyes were full of hope.
Everyone's attention fell on that photo.

glosses.notes: Usually means wood as a material or a piece of wood; in casual speech it can also compare someone to wood for being stiff or unresponsive.

examples.sentence: 这张桌子是木头做的。
院子里放着几块木头。
你怎么站着不说话，像木头一样。

example_translations.translation: This table is made of wood.
There are several pieces of wood lying in the yard.
Why are you just standing there without saying anything, like a block of wood?

glosses.notes: Introduces a condition that still will not change the result, often with a meaning like even if or no matter how.

examples.sentence: 哪怕下雨，我们也要按时出发。
哪怕只有一天，我也想回家看看。
这件事哪怕再难，也得做完。

example_translations.translation: Even if it rains, we still have to leave on time.
Even if it's only for one day, I still want to go home and have a look.
No matter how hard this matter is, it still has to be finished.

glosses.notes: Can describe something precious because it is rare, and it also often means that something happens only rarely.

examples.sentence: 大家平时都忙，今天难得坐在一起吃饭。
这是一次很难得的学习机会。
他难得早点下班，孩子特别高兴。

example_translations.translation: Everyone is usually busy, so it's rare that we're sitting together to eat today.
This is a very rare learning opportunity.
He rarely gets off work early, so the children were especially happy.

glosses.notes: Refers to how hard something is, especially a task, exercise, competition, or piece of work.

examples.sentence: 这道题的难度不算高。
老师慢慢提高了练习的难度。
这个工作的难度比我想的大。

example_translations.translation: The difficulty level of this question is not very high.
The teacher gradually increased the difficulty of the exercises.
The difficulty of this job is greater than I had expected.

glosses.notes: A formal adverb placed before another verb to mean hard to do or hard to happen.

examples.sentence: 这么大的变化让人难以接受。
她的心情难以用语言表达。
太远了，难以看清楚。

example_translations.translation: Such a big change is hard to accept.
Her feelings are difficult to express in words.
It is too far away to see clearly.

glosses.notes: A formal word for an adult male, often used in news reports, announcements, and sports labels.

examples.sentence: 那名男子在门口等了很久。
一名男子坐在树下休息。
男子组的比赛下午开始。

example_translations.translation: That man waited at the doorway for a long time.
A man was sitting under the tree resting.
The men's division competition begins in the afternoon.

glosses.notes: Often means to make noise, make a scene, or stir up trouble; in some contexts it describes a place as noisy and lively.

examples.sentence: 孩子一闹，大家都没法休息。
这里晚上太闹，我睡不着。
别因为这点小事再闹了。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the child starts making a fuss, nobody can rest.
It is too noisy here at night, so I can't sleep.
Don't keep quarreling over such a small matter.

glosses.notes: A clock or phone alarm used to wake someone up or remind them of a set time.

examples.sentence: 我把闹钟定在六点半。
早上的闹钟一响，他就坐起来了。
出差的时候，我总会带一个小闹钟。

example_translations.translation: I set the alarm clock for six thirty.
As soon as the alarm clock rang in the morning, he sat up.
When I travel for work, I always bring a small alarm clock.

glosses.notes: Refers to the inside of an object, group, or organization, or to matters that stay within it.

examples.sentence: 这个问题只在公司内部讨论。
机器内部出了点问题。
我们得先解决内部问题。

example_translations.translation: This issue is discussed only within the company.
A small problem came up inside the machine.
We have to solve the internal problems first.

glosses.notes: Describes someone who is practical, efficient, and good at getting work done.

examples.sentence: 她年轻，但是很能干。
店里那个年轻人特别能干。
大家都说他是个很能干的人。

example_translations.translation: She is young, but very capable.
That young person in the shop is especially capable.
Everyone says he is a very capable person.

glosses.notes: Refers to the first part of the year, usually around January or the early months.

examples.sentence: 我们年初就定好了今年的计划。
这家店是年初开的。
年初的时候，这里还下过大雪。

example_translations.translation: We settled this year's plan at the beginning of the year.
This shop opened early in the year.
At the beginning of the year, there was even heavy snow here.

glosses.notes: Can refer to a broad historical period or to a specific decade such as the 1980s.

examples.sentence: 这部电影讲的是上个世纪八十年代的故事。
不同年代的人想法不一样。
那是一个变化很快的年代。

example_translations.translation: This movie tells a story from the 1980s.
People from different eras think differently.
That was an era of very fast change.

glosses.notes: A common spoken word for someone's age, often used when talking about whether someone is young or old enough for something.

examples.sentence: 他年纪不大，但经验不少。
到了这个年纪，我更想过安静的生活。
你别看她年纪小，她很有自己的想法。

example_translations.translation: He isn't very old, but he has quite a bit of experience.
At this age, I want even more to live a quiet life.
She may be young, but she has very clear ideas of her own.

glosses.notes: The family meal eaten on Lunar New Year's Eve, usually when everyone tries to come home and eat together.

examples.sentence: 我们全家每年都一起吃年夜饭。
为了赶上年夜饭，他提前一天回家。
妈妈从下午就开始准备年夜饭。

example_translations.translation: Our whole family eats New Year's Eve dinner together every year.
To make it home for the reunion dinner, he went home a day early.
Mom started preparing New Year's Eve dinner in the afternoon.
